title: The minimal-model programme, and the two experiments the literature asked for

hypotheses.minimal_models: Four findings x six structural ablations. A finding's minimal model is the set of commitments whose REMOVAL kills it. Reported as a set, not a score.
hypotheses.H9.1: A learned surface detector sitting in front of the intent machinery reconciles the eye-tracking with E19 -- and it misfires on human work sharing the surface.
hypotheses.H9.2: The misfiring gets WORSE as the detector gets better, because confidence on a correlate is what produces false accusation.
hypotheses.H9.3: A pre-shut gate protects where a reactively-shut one does not. At matched engagement, adversarial reading drifts less than sympathetic reading.
hypotheses.H9.4: A 'read this differently' label protects better than a 'do not read this' label, without costing accuracy on genuine work.

nulls.N41: the label effect survives at least one ablation
nulls.N42: at least one finding dies to at least one ablation
nulls.N43: the surface detector carries no goal information
nulls.N44: adversarial mode does not protect merely by reducing engagement

fails_if.minimal_models: every ablation kills everything (N41) or nothing (N42)
fails_if.H9.2: detector accuracy and false-alarm rate move in the same direction
fails_if.H9.4: the two labels are equivalent, in which case the practical objection to the affordance -- nobody applies a 'do not look' label to their own work -- stands

not_built: the human acquisition test -- named as the top external priority, needs subjects and money
